explanation: Locate the rightmost ascent. Swap its smaller entry with the smallest larger entry in the decreasing suffix, then reverse that suffix to make it minimal. A fully nonincreasing permutation has no successor and returns an empty list.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The longest nonincreasing suffix is already in its greatest ordering, so a successor must increase the preceding pivot. Swapping it with the smallest larger suffix value makes the smallest possible increase. Reversing the remaining suffix makes the rest lexicographically minimal, producing the immediate successor.
walkthrough: For [2,1,3], the pivot is 1. Swap it with 3 and reverse the remaining one-entry suffix, obtaining [2,3,1].
edgeCases: A fully nonincreasing input has no successor and returns an empty list.
Repeated values require strict comparisons when choosing the pivot successor.
The successful result reuses and rearranges the supplied list.
